description.en: Canada observes several statutory public holidays each year that reflect its national history, bilingual identity, multicultural values, and respect for workers and veterans. These holidays influence government services, school calendars, banking operations, and workplace schedules across the country.

sections.title: About Canada
sections.content: Canada is a country in North America. Its ten provinces and three territories extend from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean and northward into the Arctic Ocean, making it the second-largest country by total area, with the longest coastline of any country. Its border with the United States is the longest international land border. The country is characterized by a wide range of both meteorologic and geological regions. With a population of over 41 million, it has widely varying population densities, with the majority residing in its urban areas and large areas being sparsely populated. Its capital is Ottawa and its three largest metropolitan areas are Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver.

sections.title: How Public Holidays Are Observed in Canada
sections.content: On statutory public holidays, federal and provincial government offices are closed. Banks and many private businesses also close or operate on reduced hours. Schools typically close nationwide, though retail observance rules vary by province.

sections.title: Why Canadaâ€™s Public Holidays Matter
sections.content: Knowning Canadaâ€™s public holidays assists with business operations, payroll planning, and academic scheduling. It is also vital for travel and accommodation planning, as well as managing official deadlines.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Canada?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Canada?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Canada?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Canada?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Canada?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
